a ZZ-tag is a very useful tool in recombinant production of proteins by E. coli.

the ZZ domain protects the target protein against proteolysis, that the ZZ domain does not compromise downstream processing and that the secretion capacity is not a major bottleneck in recombinant protein production.

the identification and elimination of the bottlenecks in the secretion of recombinant proteins by E. coli and we have demonstrated that the ZZ domain provides a very useful and versatile fusion partner for the production of proteins in E. coli.

the development of a recombinant proinsulin production system in E. coli, which has a high potential for the production of other recombinant proteins.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of the ZZ domain as an affinity handle is a good alternative for the purification of recombinant human insulin precursors.

a maximum secretion level of about 7.0 mg g(-1), a molecular weight of 24 kDa, the use of the ZZ domain as a fusion partner and a selective deletion of the ZZ domain are the best options for the secretion of proinsulin and similar fusion proteins by E. coli.
the secretion capacity is the major bottleneck in recombinant protein secretion by E. coli.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a ZZ-proinsulin fusion protein can be efficiently expressed in E. coli and that the use of a shorter ZZ fusion partner does not compromise secretion efficiency or protein stability.
secretion of ZZ-proinsulin in E. coli is limited by the secretion capacity of E. colicell, not by the molecular size or the stability of the protein in the periplasma.
the ZZ-proinsulin fusion protein is a good model for studying bottlenecks in protein secretion by E. coli.
